Subject: Dedicated capacity — integration & autoscaling follow-up

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side.

Recap (what we heard)
- You want Dedicated capacity (VPC) to host inference for the Acme chat assistant + reranker pipeline.
- Primary goals: predictable latency (p99 target ~200–250ms for assistant), cost predictability, and private networking for PHI-adjacent data.
- Typical traffic: steady-state tooling queries and day-time spikes for interactive sessions (Alex sent a quick sketch in the call).

Integration/architecture items to validate
1) SDK & auth
   - SDK quickstart (Python/JS) + service account with short-lived tokens (we support API keys, OAuth service accounts, and mTLS for Private).
   - For Dedicated we recommend issuing a service account and using our short-lived tokens tied to your KMS (we can walk through key wrapping).
2) Routing & fallbacks
   - Route by policy: latency-first for interactive sessions, cost-first for background batch jobs.
   - Automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity constrained.
3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We support function/tool calling (JSON schema) and structured output validation hooks.
   - Decide whether to use runtime tool-calling (real-time) or preprocessed actions for higher throughput.
4) Embeddings + reranker
   - Standard pattern: precompute candidate embeddings → FAISS/ANN index → candidate generation → reranker model on Dedicated.
   - Reranker can be colocated on the same Dedicated pool or run on a separate pool depending on latency needs.
5) Autoscaling, throughput & queues (high-level)
   - We need concrete numbers from you (steady QPS, peak QPS, avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, target p99/p95) to size pools.
   - Initial sizing suggestions follow in the detailed attachment.

Action items / next steps
- Alex: send sample traffic profile (CSV or summary) and confirm whether VPC/on-prem is needed (you mentioned VPC).
- Aditya/Engineering: prepare a short architecture note with SDK/auth steps and a first-pass capacity calc (I asked him to draft this).
- Lauren: provide autoscaling policy options and min/max GPU pools + queue sizing recommendations.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (first-pass numbers), rmi-autoscale-calc.xlsx (calc workbook).

I'll schedule a 60-minute architecture workshop next week once we have sample traffic. Any immediate questions, flag them here.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — adding some technical detail that will help with sizing and the workshop.

SDK & auth (practical)
- SDKs: Python/Node examples available; install with pip/npm and set REDWOOD_API_URL to your dedicated endpoint.
- Auth: For Dedicated VPC we recommend either: (A) mTLS with client certs + short-lived tokens, or (B) service account tokens bound to your KMS. Both are supported; mTLS gives strongest zero-trust posture.
- Recommended pattern: create a read-only service account for inference clients and a separate admin account for infra automation.

Routing & structured output
- Routing: policy rules are evaluated at the gateway. You can route by header (X-Route-Policy), request metadata (customer tier), or session type.
- Structured output / tool-calling: we support an explicit function-calling protocol (JSON schema). The SDK validates function signatures and will surface schema errors client-side to reduce invalid calls to the model.

Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Typical flow: index compute (batch) -> ANN index (FAISS/HNSW) -> candidate set (N=50) -> reranker (rescore top 50).
- Reranker sizing: small reranker (distil) can handle ~200 qps per GPU for short inputs; larger rerankers will need dedicated GPUs.

Autoscaling capacity calc (quick notes)
- Concurrency: for decoder-only models, concurrency per GPU is roughly inversely proportional to avg sequence length and kv-cache pressure. As a baseline: ~8–12 realtime requests per A100-80GB for 7B quantized models at ~512 context.
- Throughput: estimate tokens/sec per GPU depending on quantization and batch sizes. We'll use your sample profile to refine.
- Warm pool & queue: keep a small warm pool (min instances) to keep cold-starts low; use a queue with leaky-bucket behavior and a max queue TTL (e.g., 2s) for low-latency paths.

I attached the workbook with our quick calc (rmi-autoscale-calc.xlsx) — fill in your avg prompt/response tokens and peak qps and I’ll re-run the numbers.

Happy to jump on the architecture workshop and walk through the workbook line-by-line.

- Aditya

Traffic summary (prod target)
- Steady-state QPS: ~25 requests/sec
- Peak QPS (spiky): up to 120 requests/sec for 10–15 minute bursts twice per weekday
- Avg prompt tokens: 400 tokens
- Avg response tokens: 150 tokens
- Target p99 latency for interactive assistant: 250ms (we can accept higher for reranker batch jobs)
- Model preference: start with a 7B-class model, willing to evaluate 13B if latency allows.
- Networking: VPC preferred (we need private peering to our cloud infra).

1) Do you have a recommended min/max GPU pool for these numbers?
2) What queue behavior do you recommend when we hit burst levels? Do you drop or fall back to a cheaper model?

Alex — quick sizing and policy recommendations based on the numbers you provided. These are first-pass and we should iterate once we see the CSV.

Sizing (initial recommendation)
- Model assumption: redwood-7b-q4 (quantized) for primary path. If you test 13B, expect ~40–60% lower concurrency per GPU.
- Concurrency per A100-80GB (7B-q4): ~10 live requests at 512 context; assume 8 with 512+512 KV pressure to be conservative.
- Baseline pool (min): 3 GPUs (handles steady ~25 qps with headroom for batching and prefixes).
- Max pool: 12 GPUs (handles bursts to ~120 qps when autoscaled).

Autoscaling policy & queueing
- Policy: scale based on 95th-percentile queue wait + GPU utilization. Rapid scale-up on sustained 30s windows; slower scale-down with cooldown (5–10 min).
- Queue: leaky-bucket with max queue length 300 requests for the low-latency path and TTL 2s. After TTL expiry, fallback to: (1) smaller model variant OR (2) best-effort degraded response, depending on route policy.
- Fallback: configured as route-level policy; for premium users we prefer fallback to smaller model variant (keeps response quality acceptable); for low-tier batch jobs we queue longer or return 429.

Reranker placement
- If p99 latency requirement is strict (<=250ms) colocate reranker with inference pool. This avoids network hops.
- If reranker latency can be relaxed, run on separate cheaper pool to reduce cost.

Operational notes
- Warm pool: keep 1–2 idle instances ready for instant scale (reduces cold-start tail).
- Observability: we will surface token-level cost and per-route p99/p95 dashboards in Console.

I’ll refine these numbers after the CSV. For the workshop we can walk through a few scenarios and run the calc workbook.

Thanks,
